content: STRING (Latin stringere, to bind, to draw
tight) means bind. From here the pack takes
one root at a time and follows it out.
restrict   back + bound
constrict  together + bound
stringent  binding
district   apart + bound
Stringere came through French as estreindre
and estresse: strain, stress, distress and
strait are all the same tightening.
Prestige is praestringere, to bind the eyes
fast, to dazzle. It was a conjuror's trick
long before it was an honor.
THE NEXT 13 CARDS: string words.
VENT (Latin venire, to come) means come.
convention    together + coming
intervention  between + coming
prevention    before + coming
circumvent    around + come
An adventure is what comes toward you. A
revenant is one who comes back, and revenue
is what comes back to the treasury. A
souvenir comes up from below: a memory that
rises.
Avenue and venue are the French ways of
coming: the way toward, and the place
arrived at.
THE NEXT 13 CARDS: vent words.
CAP (Latin capere, to take) means take. It
appears as CEIVE, CEPT and CIP.
receive     back + take
perceive    thoroughly + take
intercept   between + take
anticipate  before + take
The vowel shifts when a prefix lands on it:
capere becomes -cipere, and the past form
captus becomes -cept. To deceive is to take
someone away from the truth.
Emancipate holds manus, a hand, with
capere: to release from another's hand.
THE NEXT 13 CARDS: cap words.
CAD (Latin cadere, to fall) means fall. The
past form casus, a falling, gives CAS.
accident     upon + falling
decadent     down + falling
deciduous    off + falling
coincidence  together + upon + falling
What falls upon you is an accident. What
falls together with something else is a
coincidence. Casus is also a case, the
thing that has befallen, and a casualty is
one the fall took.
A cadence is the fall of a voice at the
close of a line.
THE NEXT 13 CARDS: cad words.
PEL (Latin pellere, to drive, to push)
means drive. The past form pulsus gives
PULS.
compel      fully + drive
expel       out + drive
repel       back + drive
propulsion  forward + driving
Each of them is a push in a named
direction. A pulse is blood driven forward
by the heart; a compulsion is a push you
did not choose.
An appeal is Latin appellare, to call upon,
built on the same driving.
THE NEXT 13 CARDS: pel words.
GEN (Latin genus, generis, birth or kind;
generare, to beget) means birth, kind.
generate    to beget
regenerate  again + beget
degenerate  down + beget
progeny     forth + begotten
One root, two harvests. Birth: genesis,
progeny, congenital, and indigenous, born
within a place. Kind: gender, genre and
general. Genuine is genuinus, of the true
stock.
Genocide, coined in 1944, joins the root to
caedere, to kill.
THE NEXT 14 CARDS: gen words.
PAR is two Latin words in one shape:
parare, to make ready, and par, equal.
prepare   before + make ready
repair    again + make ready
compare   together + as equals
parity    the state of equal
Prepare, repair, separate and apparatus are
parare. Compare, parity, peer and disparage
are par, equal: a peer is one who stands
level with you.
This is the last cluster of the pack. The
roots you have met here will keep turning
up for the rest of your reading.
THE NEXT 14 CARDS: par words.
You began with aquarium and candidate and
ended with sever and imperative.
Thirty clusters, the roots two to a cluster,
and a relative on every card: five hundred
words taught and a thousand met. The famous
twenty at the front were the easy ones. The
last tier took one root at a time and
followed it as far as it goes.
The next time you meet a word you have never
seen, look for the parts. A prefix at the
front for the direction, a root in the
middle for the meaning, an ending for the
type of word. They are almost always there.
This is the last card. The system is yours.
